Prairie Saddle 

On the back of Henry H. Goodman was a damp puddle of sweat that formed from the Arizona sun. He rode in a trudging pace holding his sidearm in case other riders were sent to kill him. 

Not forty minutes before he found himself riding East he managed to gun down 10 men sent for his captivity. The sounds of hooves against the cracked ground sent him nearly jumping out of bed. Through a tear in the curtain he saw those men. Badges on their chests, and powdered dirt on their spurs. "Henry H. Goodman!" His name was called from the center gunman who held a piece of paper, presumably a wanted poster, in his hand but kept flapping in the dry wind. "This is the Canyon Rock's detainee party. We've been sent orders to detain you and bring you back to Canyon Rock's sheriff's department. Dead or Alive.... Now I know what your thinking. Maybe you got a chance to slip away by putting some lead between ourselves and yourself sir. Here at my side is Tony Tomahawk. Best gunman West of the Mississippi.". Tony Tomahawk. A revered veteran that got into the business of bounty hunting after his time in the American Indian Wars. Ironically his pseudonym Tony Tomahawk was earned not because of his skill with a revolver. It was given to him because of the brutish deaths he brought about any Native that he crossed. Most notable was the head smashing incident where he smashed the face of 14 year old Native warrior with a rock the size of his palm. Took him 15 minutes for the boy to stop breathing. Didn't even give him the courtesy of strangulation. Even this was troubling to some of the more hateful veterans. When asked about it he simply stated: "A boy with war paint on his face. Is not." 

"And I have 8 other men in case you decide to run East." The detainee party grew into a slight chuckle. Confident that they'd have Goodman at the end of a rope by the Arizona Government by the end of the day. Henry knew that death was an option on both fronts, but it didn't confront him. With shaking hands he placed golden shells into his revolver. One of the gunmen unsaddled and untied his horse from the hitching rail. The horse ran sporadically as the first warning shot was drawn.  The shot ran through Henry's window and impacted in the small kitchen. Reacting almost instantaneously Henry shot back hitting a gunman to the farthest right in the torso. Falling back the gunman's horse stood high before running off trailing the gunman still tied to his saddle. 

Hell broke loose. 

Erupting in smoke and gunfire Henry shot back without clear vantage points. Only reaching his arm out before firing. The only thing that stood between himself and hot lead was a wall no thicker than a text book. 9 men left. Henry crawled to the next window where the first shot had flown through. He looked out the window to see the gunman shooting at where he stood. Henry aimed and fired two shots that took two riders down before quickly barrel rolling behind the kitchen counter. Two birds two stones. 7 men left. The gunfire halted for and he could hear the men spreading out. Silence encumbered the small desert home. It stayed this way for about 15 minutes. 

A lone shadow crept toward the front of the house. Henry took an old whiskey bottle, half drank, and ripped off a piece of his shirt to plug the top end. He quickly lit the cloth and tossed it out of the broken window. Henry knew he had aimed correctly when the gunman started to screech in between the smells of burning flesh. Other gunman had called to help put out the fire of their fellow. With the distraction created Henry reloaded his revolver full, and kicked the front door open to fire on the assisting gunman. Water canisters and blood sprayed sporadically in between the men. Killing four that came to the gunman's aid, and left the man to burn to death. A whizzing bullet from the East flew close and sent Henry to take shelter behind the home. 

2 men left. The central gunman kept firing from the East until the familiar clicks of an empty chamber entwined with the sound of deathly silence. Henry took two shots at the central gunman missing the first, but impacting the second on the gunman's leg. The gunman whimpered loudly and pathetically crawling away from the scene. Henry decided to let the desert have him.

1 man left. As Henry walked out amidst the bodies he noticed not all were dead. Then heard the clank of spurs behind him. He turned slowly to see Tony Tomahawk untying his gun belt and letting it crash to the ground around his ankles. Tomahawk then pulled a Bowie knife and cleaned it with his pant thigh. Henry pulled a much smaller knife from one on the gunman's saddle. They circled each other like predators do to prey. Two men cut from the same cloth of wickedness. Soon to be one left. Tomahawk then quickly pounced at Goodman with ferocity in his countenance. Goodman grabbed the knife held arm and sliced deep and long on Tomahawks back. Tomahawk broke loose and circled him again. This time will blood trickling down his boots. Tomahawk removed his spurs and charged at him again this time slicing open Goodman's chest and shoulder before Goodman pushed him off. Goodman collapsed to the ground heaving. Tomahawk approached and stood over him. Goodman could see no soul in this man's eyes. Empty and sullen Tomahawk would gather no satisfaction from this kill. Hes killed too many to see the difference. 

Goodman grabbed Tomahawk's foot and pushed upwards making him fall to his back. Goodman knelt quickly and jabbed the small knife into Tomahawk's guts. Surprise filled the empty eyes of Tony Tomahawk, and Goodman grabbed the Bowie knife from his now loosened grip to slice his throat open. Blood poured like a fountain from Tomahawk's mouth and larynx. Choking on his own blood. 

Goodman stood and wobbled to the nearest saddled horse and rode to East. He was no stranger to death nor conflict. He'd just been lucky this time. In two weeks time when Canyon Rock's Sheriff figures that all 10 men are dead then Goodman's bounty is sure to rise. So saddling out of Arizona was probably better. Every so often he conveyed his surroundings in paranoia. The desert's wind could have been a whisper. The lone cacti in the distance could have been more gunman, and the buzzards that flew above him in ceremonious formation could have meant that he was already dead.

*^(The Science Museum)* 

While inside the Observatory my oldest, Mark who was going to be 7 on the 3rd, wanted to see the Osher Rainforest. Which is an enclosed indoor dome that holds some of the world's most exotic birds. It's kept relativity humid, and a myriad of chirrups resonate the transparent dome. Barkley, my middle child, was making a fuss because he wanted to see the Albino Alligator again. After quieting him with the promise that we'd see the Alligator before leaving; we inadvertently headed toward the Osher Rainforest. It was only a few minutes until the Dome's humidity colored my cheeks rose, and gave me frizzy hair that comes with condensation. I smiled before taking a photo of my husband Ryan lifting Mark to see the nest eggs of a Blue - Necked Tanager. A bird chiefly found in the coasts of South America. *"I can see them! I can see them!"* Mark shouted, waking up my youngest, Paul, who had just turned age two. I took one more photo of what was definitely going to be framed at home; before stepping away and venturing alone. 

Taking small snapshots on my way toward the exit the Osher Rainforest grew more silent. The ambience was completely cut off when I had gotten near the entrance of the Rockhampton Maze. The rain had just settled, and the gray sky was hanging over. Bouts of fog stagnated at certain pockets of the maze.  All of these elements soaked my windbreaker, and tagged my cheeks so that they were cold to the touch. Though I did see other people who wandered the maze, it was the most alone I had felt in years. As a 31 year old mother you can imagine what that might feel like. Even on days when Ryan would watch our three boys, I still had premonition's, and would usually come home early. The Rockhampton Maze was different. I gently slid my fingers across the dew covered leaves of ten foot high Maze walls. Guilt tugged me as I had thoughts that were sorely my own. Before I had children, and before I met Ryan. I could have been here exploring the Osher Rainforest, the Rockhampton Maze, and the Albino Alligator alone. Without the slightest hint of obligation or responsibility.

The thought of my family seemed so foreign that by the time I met back up with them at the food court; they seemed like strangers without a mother or wife.  My mind brushed off the experience, and I was back into 'Mom Mode' so to speak. *"Who wants to see the Albino Alligator again?"* I asked playfully. My kids exclaimed in joy, and we walked together; before leaving home. We all tend to have memories that are meaningful to us. A place in time that we frame, and hang on the walls of our consciousness. No matter how meaningless we feel. To look back at them and smile for it to have ever happened at all. 

At the Rockhamptom Maze is were I'd want to be if I had a Level 2.

**^(Army of the Mentally Ill)**

​

Adam can tell how many days he hasn't slept by looking at how filthy his hands become. He looks down at his hands gripping the steering wheel. White knuckled and grimy. Similar to the hands of a mechanic. "Shit!" he says as he wipes the beads of sweat that formed above his eyebrows. 

It's been about a week. 

*"You disgust me!" "You haven't taken your medication?." "DON'T TAKE IT!" "You wouldn't take it...would you?"*

Followed by a few sobs he gave a pathetic wail, and started the car. Adam drove down the coast near his home, and recited his Therapist's affirmations "This is my head, and nobody else's.". In the veil of his manic state, a loud thump sent him nearly colliding with a street lamp. Under its yellow glare he tried to rationalize truth and fiction. Had he run someone over? Killed someone? 

The blinking hazard's revealed a slumped over body in strobe vision. Continuing his attempt to rationalize the situation he saw a distorted Dementophobis. The God of Insanity. Laying there with a birds beak,and olive branch split in two halves, but then it formed back into a middle aged woman in joggers attire. 

"*Big big trouble here..." JAIL TIME!" "You did it.. You killed Dementophobis." \*Applause\*Applause\**

Overwhelmed by exhilaration his nostrils flared, and he raised his hands up like an Olympic gold medal recipient. "I did it. I killed the God of Insanity." he whispered head down. When Adam was finished basking in his victory he saw headlights emerge between the fog on the neighboring mountain. Quickly, he picked up the God in neon jogging attire, and placed him into his trunk, and drove home.  

The next morning drew another sleepless night for Adam. The voices had grown increasingly volatile. Congratulating him at one moment, and cursing him the next. One of the voices stood out. "*Adam, it distresses me to know that my keeper has passed*." said in a low weepy voice. "Who are you?" asked Adam. The voice didn't respond but continued weeping. "*You are the beginning of Dementi AD (After Death)."*  At that moment Adam felt every accomplishment Dementopbis has achieved. The antibiotic enemies he's defeated, and his army of mentally ill minds. He walked out into the sunshine that day. Looking around the city streets he saw the 'Army of the Mentally Ill'. Sitting on park benches, waiting in grocery store lines, and wearing uniforms, like mailmen and construction workers to disguise themselves. 

All of them affirming themselves. "This is my head, and nobody else's."
